- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values by 1–2% relative to sentiment-driven highs.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to account for mean reversion.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment — dampen early forecast spikes by 0.3–0.7% for each lagged period.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish (0.3–0.5), reduce forecast volatility — avoid sharp upward moves unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive positive sentiment shifts.
- Forecast mean reversion bias is strongest in 10–15 day horizons — apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction to mid-term forecasts if recent price action shows consolidation.
- Overshoots after strong bullish sentiment (sentiment > 0.7) are common — cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2.0% below the 30-day moving average of prior 5 days.
